newsitem.title: USA: Report says Pa. Pike should use bids for attorneys.
newsitem.headline: Report says Pa. Pike should use bids for attorneys.

text.p: A legislative audit recommended that Pennsylvania Turnpike use competitive bids to select bond attorneys, Philadelphia Inquirer reported Wednesday.
Currently, the agency steers bond counsel work to politically connected law firms, splitting fees evenly between Democrat and Republican lawyers, the newspaper said.
The report, by the staff of the Legislature's Legislative Budget and Finance Committe, said competitive bids could save the agency tens of thousands of dollars on every bond deal.
Five of six neighboring states use competitive bids to pick bond counsel, and generally pay much less for the service than the Pennsylvania Turnpike, the report said.
The Turnpike's executive director, John Durbin, said the agency does not agree with the report's conclusions, arguing that negotiating fees with law firms can yield fair prices.
